n1.text: Home → Pick → Create is POST /api/sessions {gameType, nickname, password?, settings?}. Join is POST /:code/join. Both hand back playerId + playerToken — keep the token and the code in localStorage, it is the only identity there is.

n2.text: These three screens are one phase field: game.round.phase = answering → revealed → resolved. Which of them a player sees also depends on whether they are round.activePlayerId. Button visibility comes from canSetQuestion / canReveal / canForceReveal / canPickResult / canGoNext — never recompute the rules on the client.

n3.text: One gap versus the brief: the API has no route from revealed straight to the next asker. pickResult (winner + loser) is what moves a round to resolved, and only then does nextRound rotate. So the pick screen is in — it is also where the scoreboard comes from. If you want pure reveal-and-move-on, that is an API change: a skipResult action, or a settings flag that auto-resolves.
